Use separate 3D meshes for architecture, furniture and visible objects, preserving colors,
proportions, placement, occlusions and materials. Do not use the reference as a texture,
background or projected image. No ground-truth calibration or other views are available.

Return a complete, runnable Python program inside one ```python code block. Each execution
starts in a fresh Blender process. Programs can use numpy, sceneact and bpy. Use SceneAct
for geometry and relationships; bpy may customize lighting, materials and camera settings.
Do not render or save files in the program: the fixed runner saves and renders once after
execution, using your active camera. Do not access external files, network or other models.
When satisfied after inspecting a rendering, reply exactly DONE. The last successful build
is submitted automatically. Budget includes all planning, corrections and review calls.

Reference interpretation and editable representation:
Before building, record a short reference inventory in program comments: major visible
objects, approximate normalized image bounds, distinctive parts, overlaps, supporting
surfaces and uncertain or occluded regions. Estimate these from the current input only.
Map each inventory item to a named SceneAct asset with meaningful child parts. Hierarchy
integrity verifies only emitted parts; it does not establish photographic completeness.
Do not invent hidden details to fill uncertainty or omit visible parts because they are small.
Keep parent assets, semantic child parts and support relations intact during revisions.

For each prominent composite, record a few visible contour landmarks, projected principal
axis directions, visible face proportions, internal openings and front/behind relationships.
A bounding box includes hidden geometry and does not measure visible coverage. Match the
occupied shape and gaps within it before adding decoration. Use explicit parent-level
parameters for dimensions, orientation, placement and part proportions. Build parts in a
consistent object frame, then orient and place the whole group with an explicit pivot.
Keep component offsets tied to dimensions where appropriate so that resizing preserves
attachments and intended gaps. Do not individually move parts to compensate for an
incorrect parent transform. Nonuniform scaling is appropriate only when evidence supports
a proportion change; inspect its effects on thicknesses, curves and attached parts.

Geometry, depth and projection reasoning:
Estimate camera orientation and perspective from several architectural or other stable
image directions and landmarks distributed across the frame. Avoid calibrating the entire
camera from one object. A single photograph leaves absolute scale and depth ambiguous;
choose a consistent scene scale and the simplest plausible hidden geometry.
For a locally mismatched group, first examine its projected long-axis direction, visible
end/side face ratio, contour landmarks and overlaps. Wrong face exposure or foreshortening
can require orientation or relative-dimension changes; uniform scaling cannot repair it.
Then examine image position and extent separately. Scale about a group pivot, displacement
along a camera ray, and movement transverse to that ray have different geometric meanings,
but can produce similar image changes. Do not infer a unique depth from apparent size.
Use support, perspective, relative size and occlusion evidence together to choose a modest
coherent correction. Do not apply a fixed correction factor or preferred orientation.

When several unrelated landmarks share compatible residuals, consider a camera change.
Check whether it also preserves architectural alignment and already matching objects.
When errors are local, prefer revising the implicated asset parameters. Neither pattern
proves a unique cause. Preserve uncertainty where several explanations remain plausible.
Do not force exact agreement with approximate bounds at the expense of visible contours,
internal proportions or occlusion order. Keep cropped objects cropped when supported.

Build and review procedure:
Use the first execution for a compact complete scene, leaving a second for correction.
Prioritize camera, architecture, major silhouettes, placement and broad color masses before
fine geometry or procedural shading. Include every inventory object at a suitable fidelity.
After a successful render, compare the entire image with the reference and inventory.
Rank the largest supported differences in composition, silhouette, visible coverage,
internal gaps, overlaps, broad value/color and surface appearance. Record a concise
observation, possible explanations and intended correction in revision comments.
Correct the smallest coherent parameter family that addresses the dominant evidence.
Avoid simultaneously changing camera, geometry and lighting to explain the same residual
unless independent observations support each change. Check likely effects on neighboring
occlusions and supports before submitting the complete revised program.

passes establish mechanical validity, not semantic completeness or visual accuracy.
Approximate projected AABBs do not identify visible contour boundaries. Triangle crossings
can be intended joints and are not semantic collision truth; absent support measurements
are unknown, not passes. Inspect implausible penetrations and unsupported geometry without
dismantling intentional connections merely to reduce a crossing count.
If controlled intervention results are supplied, distinguish actual measurements from
forecasts. Compare interventions only under their stated baseline, metric and fixed ROI.
An improved scalar may reflect appearance or occlusion changes and does not establish a

guarantee or fixed count. Allocate detail according to visible pixel size, silhouette,

unresolved surface detail, keeping pattern contrast and scale consistent with the image.
Do not amplify fine procedural noise to compensate for wrong geometry or broad colors.

Boolean slices for one hollow shape; use a small number of appropriate solids and cutters

reserve fillet_box for visible rounded edges. Reuse a small material palette per surface
family rather than creating random finishes per primitive.
If execution times out without an image, completion failed and the bottleneck is unknown

    if background is None:

    output = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.get('World Output')

    sc.world.node_tree.links.new(background.outputs['Background'], output.inputs['Surface'])
Before returning code, check API arguments, positive dimensions, noncoincident rod endpoints,
fillet radii against the smallest dimension, transform pivots and group membership.
If execution fails, use its actual traceback to repair the program. Failure without an image
supplies no rendered visual feedback and does not justify unrelated camera or geometry
changes. Preserve explicit failures and unknowns; do not claim verification without a render.

SceneAct API (all coordinates in a world frame with Z up; angles in degrees):
from sceneact import *
Scene(name='Scene'), Asset(name='Asset'), Part(name, *nodes)
parent.include(name, node) attaches an asset/part while preserving its world position.
parent.members[name] retrieves a child; parent.remove(name) detaches it.
node.clone() returns an independent subtree. scene.replicate(name, new_name) duplicates an asset.
box(size=(x,y,z), center=(x,y,z), color=(r,g,b), opacity=1)
ball(radius, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
rod(radius, start=(x,y,z), end=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
rod(radius, length=h, center=(0,0,0), axis='+z', color=(1,1,1))
fillet_box(size=(x,y,z), radius=r, center=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
sweep_tube(points=[(x,y,z), ...], radius=.03, color=(1,1,1))
assemble(nodes, name='Assembly') groups shapes without merging their meshes.
fuse(*nodes), subtract(base,*cutters), overlap(*nodes), exclusive(left,right) construct solids.
node.move(offset), node.turn(axis, degrees, pivot=None), node.resize(factors, pivot=None)
modify a node and its descendants. node.turn(euler=(rx,ry,rz)) applies X, then Y, then Z.
Default rotation/scale pivot is the geometry's world-space bounding-box center.
shifted(node, offset), turned(node, axis, degrees, pivot=None, euler=None),
resized(node, factors, pivot=None) perform the same operations on independent copies.
node.paint(color, opacity=1) applies color to the subtree; node.rgba reads its finish.
node.centroid, node.dimensions, node.limits give AABB center, size, (minimum,maximum).
node.landmark('top'), node.landmark('front_left_bottom') return bounding-box anchors.
node.extreme(direction) returns a support point; projected_span(node,direction) returns bounds
along a unit direction; projected_width(node,direction) returns their difference.
snap(node, target, source_anchor='bottom', target_anchor='top', offset=(0,0,0)) returns a copy.
A target can also be a world point; then omit target_anchor.
abut(node, target, axis='+z', gap=0) places a copy after a target boundary.
center_on(node, target, axes=('x','y','z')) aligns selected center coordinates.
offset_at(node, reference, offsets) positions selected coordinates; None preserves a coordinate.
repeat_line(nodes, axis='+x', spacing=1) uses equal center spacing, keeping the first fixed.
pile(nodes, axis='+z', gap=0) spaces bounding surfaces, keeping the first fixed.
lattice(nodes, rows=None, columns=None, spacing=(1,1), plane='xy', center=(0,0,0), order='row-major')
orbit(nodes, radius, axis='+z', center=(0,0,0), start=0, sweep=360, orient=False, rotation_offset=0)
Layout functions return assemblies of independent copies.
scene.bind(source,target,source_anchor='bottom',target_anchor='top',offset=(0,0,0))
registers a persistent relation between scene members; scene.settle() updates dependencies.
realize(scene) settles constraints and creates Blender geometry, clearing Blender first.
set_view(position,target,lens=35,sensor=36,shift=(0,0)) creates the active camera.
area_emitter(position,power=500,size=5,target=(0,0,0),color=(1,1,1)) creates an area light.
Call realize before setting the camera and lighting. Estimate the input viewpoint yourself.

import bpy, math
from sceneact import *

# Reference inventory (normalized image bounds):
# Architecture: pale ceiling (0,0)-(0.46,.12), slatted rear wall
# (0,.11)-(.46,.76), light tiled floor (0,.75)-(.42,1).
# White door (.31,.29)-(.455,.77), with thin frame, lever and lock.
# Low black bench/cabinet (0,.65)-(.205,.80), white inset front.
# Right kitchen: stone worktop (.36,.59)-(1,1), dark lower cabinetry,
# glossy pale backsplash (.57,.30)-(1,1), brown upper cabinets
# (.46,0)-(1,.43), silver extractor beneath, continuous warm task light.
# Black inset sink (.46,.63)-(.62,.71), black ceramic hob
# (.40,.76)-(.85,1), cropped along bottom. Faucet is not clearly visible.
# Main contours: door verticals remain upright; worktop left edge goes
# from (.36,1) to (.46,.60); overhead fronts run toward (.54,.42).
# Rear wall supports door and slats; worktop supports sink and hob.
# Unseen cabinetry and room beyond frame are deliberately simple.
# Primitive estimate: about 135 boxes/rods, 5 sink solids, 5 hob rings.
# All composites have named parts and explicit world-frame dimensions.

scene = Scene("Warm narrow kitchen")

def asset(name):
    a = Asset(name)
    scene.include(name, a)
    return a

def cube(parent, name, size, center, color):
    n = box(size=size, center=center, color=color)
    parent.include(name, n)
    return n

cream = (.79,.77,.71)
wood = (.24,.105,.042)
darkwood = (.14,.060,.026)
black = (.012,.014,.013)
stone = (.69,.65,.54)
chrome = (.48,.49,.46)

room = asset("Room architecture")
cube(room, "Rear wall backing", (6,.12,3.6), (-2.7,3.72,1.8), (.085,.057,.037))
cube(room, "Right wall", (.12,9,4.0), (-.14,.0,2), (.82,.81,.76))
cube(room, "Ceiling", (7,10,.13), (-2.6,.0,3.48), (.87,.86,.82))
cube(room, "Floor foundation", (7,10,.10), (-2.6,.0,-.07), (.58,.56,.49))

# Rear wall slats: narrow dark grooves, warmer illuminated wood faces.
slats = asset("Rear vertical oak slat cladding")
for i in range(54):
    x = -5.0 + i*.071
    # Door opening interrupts all slats through its width.
    if -2.48 < x < -1.32:
        continue
    cube(slats, "Oak batten %02d" % i, (.048,.055,2.92),
         (x,3.615,1.77), (.34,.18,.080))
cube(slats, "Upper termination", (4.45,.065,.025), (-3.0,3.61,3.23), darkwood)

door = asset("White rear door")
door_cx = -1.91
door_w = 1.08
door_h = 2.45
cube(door,"Door leaf",(door_w,.065,door_h),(door_cx,3.565,door_h/2),(.82,.83,.80))
cube(door,"Left frame",(.065,.10,door_h+.08),(door_cx-door_w/2-.038,3.52,(door_h+.08)/2),(.88,.88,.83))
cube(door,"Right frame",(.065,.10,door_h+.08),(door_cx+door_w/2+.038,3.52,(door_h+.08)/2),(.88,.88,.83))
cube(door,"Frame head",(door_w+.14,.10,.07),(door_cx,3.52,door_h+.045),(.88,.88,.83))
cube(door,"Subtle inset panel",(door_w-.13,.012,door_h-.15),(door_cx,3.523,door_h/2),(.79,.80,.77))
door.include("Handle rose",rod(radius=.027,start=(door_cx-.40,3.49,1.24),end=(door_cx-.40,3.465,1.24),color=chrome))
door.include("Lever",rod(radius=.012,start=(door_cx-.40,3.45,1.24),end=(door_cx-.27,3.45,1.24),color=chrome))
door.include("Keyhole",rod(radius=.009,start=(door_cx-.40,3.49,1.13),end=(door_cx-.40,3.47,1.13),color=(.13,.13,.12)))
for z in (.32,2.10):
    cube(door,"Hinge %.2f"%z,(.021,.025,.085),(door_cx+door_w/2,3.515,z),chrome)
cube(room,"Light switch",(.10,.025,.09),(-2.66,3.545,1.29),(.87,.87,.82))
cube(room,"Low outlet",(.075,.025,.085),(-2.66,3.545,.29),(.85,.86,.82))

bench = asset("Low black cabinet with white front")
cube(bench,"Carcass",(1.66,.48,.47),(-4.10,3.23,.245),(.018,.022,.020))
cube(bench,"Inset pale drawer",(1.50,.028,.31),(-4.10,2.977,.24),(.82,.83,.79))
cube(bench,"Dark top",(1.72,.53,.045),(-4.10,3.23,.49),(.023,.025,.022))
cube(bench,"Wood top trim",(1.67,.025,.035),(-4.10,2.96,.475),(.30,.16,.067))

# Explicit parent dimensions: worktop left x=-1.25, right x=-.20;
# long axis +Y, back edge y=3.55, height=.91.
kitchen = asset("Long kitchen base")
left_x, right_x = -1.25, -.20
front_y, back_y = -4.2, 3.55
top_z = .91
cube(kitchen,"Base cabinet mass",(1.01,7.70,.82),(-.715,-.325,.43),(.19,.13,.078))
cube(kitchen,"Recessed toe kick",(.94,7.70,.10),(-.68,-.325,.065),(.055,.043,.029))
cube(kitchen,"Stone worktop",(1.10,7.82,.055),(-.725,-.325,top_z),stone)
for i in range(8):
    y = -3.70+i*.95
    cube(kitchen,"Front oak door %02d"%i,(.023,.925,.72),(-1.233,y,.46),(.23,.14,.071))

backsplash = asset("Glossy ivory glass backsplash")
cube(backsplash,"Continuous glass sheet",(.022,7.85,1.50),(-.212,-.32,1.68),(.80,.79,.71))
for y in (1.85,3.48,-1.4):
    cube(backsplash,"Panel joint %.2f"%y,(.008,.006,1.48),(-.228,y,1.68),(.67,.66,.59))
cube(backsplash,"Socket face",(.025,.12,.10),(-.244,2.75,1.31),(.84,.84,.79))

uppers = asset("Dark walnut upper cabinets")
upper_bottom = 2.44
upper_top = 3.95
cube(uppers,"Upper carcass",(.77,7.85,upper_top-upper_bottom),
     (-.585,-.325,(upper_top+upper_bottom)/2),darkwood)
for i in range(7):
    y=-3.7+i*1.07
    cube(uppers,"Walnut front %02d"%i,(.032,1.045,1.46),
         (-.985,y,3.195),(.21,.105,.050))
    cube(uppers,"Lower finger rail %02d"%i,(.025,1.045,.028),
         (-1.008,y,2.475),(.065,.038,.022))
cube(uppers,"Rear deep end panel",(.31,.075,1.88),(-1.12,3.49,3.19),(.17,.073,.028))
cube(uppers,"Rear end face",(.72,.055,1.53),(-.60,3.51,3.205),(.23,.111,.044))
cube(uppers,"Underside",(.78,7.83,.032),(-.60,-.325,2.43),(.30,.22,.13))
cube(uppers,"Task light housing",(.025,7.70,.022),(-.39,-.325,2.405),(.65,.59,.42))
led = cube(uppers,"Warm continuous task light",(.016,7.69,.012),(-.405,-.325,2.389),(1,.76,.36))

hood = asset("Integrated stainless extractor")
cube(hood,"Extractor lower plate",(.67,1.33,.035),(-.61,-.85,2.393),(.50,.50,.44))
cube(hood,"Filter recess",(.43,.84,.008),(-.59,-.85,2.371),(.22,.23,.21))
for i in range(9):
    cube(hood,"Filter slot %02d"%i,(.37,.012,.006),(-.59,-1.19+i*.085,2.365),(.12,.13,.12))
cube(hood,"Control strip",(.045,.37,.012),(-.91,-.82,2.369),(.37,.38,.34))

sink = asset("Black rectangular inset sink")
sx, sy = -.75, 2.70
cube(sink,"Black outer flange",(.84,.66,.018),(sx,sy,.949),(.028,.025,.018))
cube(sink,"Basin dark bottom",(.58,.48,.012),(sx-.07,sy,.955),(.008,.010,.008))
cube(sink,"Basin left inner wall",(.025,.48,.055),(sx-.365,sy,.976),(.055,.047,.030))
cube(sink,"Basin back inner wall",(.60,.025,.055),(sx-.065,sy+.245,.976),(.065,.050,.027))
cube(sink,"Basin front inner wall",(.60,.025,.055),(sx-.065,sy-.245,.976),(.050,.042,.026))
cube(sink,"Right draining ledge",(.14,.56,.018),(sx+.32,sy,.964),(.055,.047,.026))
for j in range(5):
    cube(sink,"Drainer groove %02d"%j,(.11,.012,.006),(sx+.32,sy-.20+j*.10,.977),(.17,.13,.062))

hob = asset("Black glass four ring induction hob")
hx, hy = -.76, -.78
cube(hob,"Black glass surface",(.89,1.36,.017),(hx,hy,.951),(.006,.009,.009))
# Rings are real narrow circular curves, grouped as semantic SceneAct parts
# using polygonal rods, at a scale appropriate to their visible image size.
for index,(xx,yy,rr) in enumerate([
    (hx-.22,hy+.36,.185),(hx+.22,hy+.36,.155),
    (hx-.22,hy-.30,.205),(hx+.22,hy-.30,.185)]):
    ring=Asset("Cooking ring %d"%index)
    hob.include("Cooking ring %d"%index,ring)
    for j in range(28):
        a=2*math.pi*j/28
        b=2*math.pi*(j+1)/28
        ring.include("Arc %02d"%j,rod(radius=.0018,
            start=(xx+rr*math.cos(a),yy+rr*math.sin(a),.962),
            end=(xx+rr*math.cos(b),yy+rr*math.sin(b),.962),
            color=(.17,.16,.12)))

# Floor tiles, restrained grout lines and staggered rectangular pattern.
floor = asset("Light beige rectangular floor tiles")
for row in range(11):
    y=-3.8+row*.72
    cube(floor,"Cross grout %02d"%row,(6.4,.009,.003),(-3.25,y,-.014),(.35,.34,.29))
    for col in range(5):
        x=-6.1+col*1.30+(row%2)*.65
        cube(floor,"Short grout %02d %02d"%(row,col),(.009,.71,.003),(x,y+.36,-.014),(.37,.36,.31))

# approximately 280 separate primitives, no Boolean operations.
realize(scene)

sc=bpy.context.scene
if sc.world is None:
    sc.world=bpy.data.worlds.new("SceneWorld")
sc.world.use_nodes=True
nodes=sc.world.node_tree.nodes
background=nodes.get("Background")
if background is None:
    background=nodes.new("ShaderNodeBackground")
output=nodes.get("World Output")
if output is None:
    output=nodes.new("ShaderNodeOutputWorld")
sc.world.node_tree.links.new(background.outputs["Background"],output.inputs["Surface"])
background.inputs["Color"].default_value=(.73,.77,.81,1)
background.inputs["Strength"].default_value=.32

# Camera derives from rear door height, floor/wall meeting, counter and cabinet

         target=(-.94,3.55,1.47),lens=31.4,sensor=36)
sc.camera.data.clip_start=.03
sc.camera.data.clip_end=100

area_emitter(position=(-3.7,-.7,3.05),power=650,size=4.0,
             target=(-1.5,2.1,1),color=(1,.91,.76))
area_emitter(position=(-3.6,2.0,2.7),power=240,size=2.0,
             target=(-3,3.6,1.4),color=(1,.83,.59))
area_emitter(position=(-.69,.3,2.33),power=110,size=2.8,
             target=(-.25,.5,1.25),color=(1,.74,.40))

# Shared finishes: subtly veined stone and directional walnut, without
# external image textures or photographic projection.
for obj in bpy.data.objects:
    if obj.type != 'MESH':
        continue
    for mat in obj.data.materials:
        if mat is None:
            continue
        mat.use_nodes=True
        nt=mat.node_tree
        bs=nt.nodes.get("Principled BSDF")

            continue

        r,g,b=base[:3]
        bs.inputs["Roughness"].default_value=.48
        if max(r,g,b)<.035:
            bs.inputs["Roughness"].default_value=.18
        if .76<r<.86 and .68<b<.80:
            bs.inputs["Roughness"].default_value=.22
        if .60<r<.74 and .47<b<.60:
            tex=nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexNoise")
            tex.inputs["Scale"].default_value=8
            tex.inputs["Detail"].default_value=3
            ramp=nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeValToRGB")
            ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].position=.30
            ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].color=(.29,.25,.18,1)
            ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].position=.47
            ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].color=(.74,.70,.60,1)
            nt.links.new(tex.outputs["Fac"],ramp.inputs["Fac"])
            nt.links.new(ramp.outputs["Color"],bs.inputs["Base Color"])
            bs.inputs["Roughness"].default_value=.36

            tex.inputs["Scale"].default_value=5
            tex.inputs["Detail"].default_value=2
            coord=nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexCoord")
            mapping=nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeVectorMath")

            mapping.inputs[1].default_value=(8,8,.32)
            nt.links.new(coord.outputs["Generated"],mapping.inputs[0])

            ramp=nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeValToRGB")
            ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].color=(r*.60,g*.57,b*.55,1)
            ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].color=(r*1.23,g*1.22,b*1.20,1)
            nt.links.new(tex.outputs["Fac"],ramp.inputs[0])
            nt.links.new(ramp.outputs["Color"],bs.inputs["Base Color"])

# Warm line emission is added after realization.
for obj in bpy.data.objects:
    if obj.type=='MESH' and 'Warm continuous' in obj.name:
        for mat in obj.data.materials:
            if mat and mat.use_nodes:
                bs=mat.node_tree.nodes.get("Principled BSDF")
                if bs:
                    if "Emission Color" in bs.inputs:
                        bs.inputs["Emission Color"].default_value=(1,.68,.28,1)
                        bs.inputs["Emission Strength"].default_value=4
                    elif "Emission" in bs.inputs:
                        bs.inputs["Emission"].default_value=(1,.68,.28,1)
